Worked solution

First, we need to recall that we can’t do the integral as long as there is a point of discontinuity for the integrand between the limits of integration. Therefore, we’ll need to replace the point of discontinuity with a parameter \(t\) as follows,

\[\displaystyle \int_{{@lower_limit@}}^{{@upper_limit@}}{@expr_udv@}\,dx =\lim_{t \to\{@const1@}} \displaystyle \int_{t}^{{@upper_limit@}}{@expr_udv@}\,dx\]

We now need to use the integration by parts technique to evaluate the integral. The formula for integration by parts is given by \[\displaystyle \int udv=u\cdot v-\int vdu\]

We now need to carefully consider the integrand and make a choice for \(u\) and \(dv\) that will simplify the integral.

Let \(u={@expr_u@}\) and \(dv={@expr_dv@}\,dx\)

\(u={@expr_u@} \, \Rightarrow du={@expr_du@}\,dx\)

\(dv={@expr_dv@}\,dx \, \Leftarrow v={@expr_v@}\)

\[ \begin{align} \displaystyle\int_{t}^{{@upper_limit@}}{@expr_udv@}\,dx &=\left[{@expr_uv@} \right]_{t}^{{@upper_limit@}}+ \int_{t}^{{@upper_limit@}} {@expr_vdu@}\,dx \\ & ={@expr_inta@} -{@expr_intb@} \\ &= {@expr_int_t@} \end{align} \]

We now need to apply L'Hospitals rule to evaluate the limit as \(t\to{@const1@}\):

\[\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0}\, t^2 ln(a*t)=0\]

Applying this rule into the integral, we get:

\[ \begin{align} \displaystyle \int_{{@lower_limit@}}^{{@upper_limit@}}{@expr_udv@}\,dx &=\lim_{t \to \infty}{@expr_int_t@}\\ &={@ta1@}\\ \end{align} \]

Therefore, the integral converges
